title: Where your toilet water goes
description: Follow one flush from your toilet, under your house, through the sewer main, a lift station and a treatment plant, back to the river.

beats.text: Ever wondered where your toilet water goes after you flush?
It drops straight down into a pipe under your house,
then turns and heads away from the building.
If it just stopped here, your garden would be a swamp.
So the pipe keeps going, always angled slightly downhill,
because flat pipes clog. Gravity does the pushing.
Under the front yard it reaches the street,
and joins a much bigger pipe: the sewer main.
Every house on your street connects to the same one.
Toilets, showers, sinks, all of it ends up here,
and the main collects it from the whole neighbourhood.
It keeps following the slope of the land,
until it's too deep to go any further. That's where a lift station comes in.
A pump sits at the bottom and pushes the sewage up a pipe,
high enough for gravity to take over again.
Eventually everything arrives at the treatment plant.
First, metal bars catch the big stuff: wipes, rags, plastic.
Then the flow slows down so sand and grit sink.
In big round tanks, the heavier sludge sinks to the bottom,
and a slow arm scrapes it away.
Next, air is pumped in to feed billions of bacteria,
that eat the dissolved waste you can't even see.
The bacteria settle out, and the water on top is almost clean.
A last pass under UV light kills what's left,
before it flows back into the river.
All of that, every time you flush.
